questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line in Parametric Form and a Plane in Cartesian Form
questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=4+3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=-2+6t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:2x+5y+8z=229.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+5y+8z & =229 \\ 2(4+3t)+5(3+4t)+8(-2+6t) & =229 \\ 8+6t+15+20t-16+48t & =229 \\ 74t & =222 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4+3(3)=13 \\ y=3+4(3)=15 \\ z=-2+6(3)=16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(13,15,16).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms
questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,5,9⟩+t⟨4,-1,6⟩,\,Π:-2x+4y+2z-16=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+4t,5-t,9+6t⟩.
$$

Let's also write the equation of the plane in the dot product form:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+4y+2z-16 & =0 \\ -2x+4y+2z & =16 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,4,2⟩ & =16 \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,4,2⟩ & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+4t,5-t,9+6t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-2,4,2⟩ & =16 \\ ⟨3+4t,5-t,9+6t⟩\cdot ⟨-2,4,2⟩ & =16 \\ -2(3+4t)+4(5-t)+2(9+6t) & =16 \\ -6-8t+20-4t+18+12t & =16 \\ 32 & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation has no solution. Therefore, we conclude that the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ do not intersect.

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=5-2t \\ y=-1+4t \\ z=-3-5t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:2x-5y+3z-84=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-5y+3z-84 & =0 \\ 2(5-2t)-5(-1+4t)+3(-3-5t) & =84 \\ 10-4t+5-20t-9-15t & =84 \\ -39t & =78 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-2$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-2(-2)=9 \\ y=-1+4(-2)=-9 \\ z=-3-5(-2)=7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(9,-9,7).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=4+2t \\ y=-3+4t \\ z=5t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:3x+2y-z=33.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+2y-z & =33 \\ 3(4+2t)+2(-3+4t)-(5t) & =33 \\ 12+6t-6+8t-5t & =33 \\ 9t & =27 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4+2(3)=10 \\ y=-3+4(3)=9 \\ z=5(3)=15\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(10,9,15).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line and a Plane Given in Other Forms
questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y}{4}=\frac{1-z}{2},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩=-9.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(-2,0,1)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨3,4,-2⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨-2,0,1⟩+t⟨3,4,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩ & =-9 \\ ⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩ & =-9 \\ 4(-2+3t)-3(4t)+(1-2t) & =-9 \\ -8+12t-12t+1-2t & =-9 \\ -2t & =-2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-2+3(1),4(1),1-2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,4,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(1,4,-1).$
